We are targeting the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on dashboard. Join us if you value a structured, collaborative environment where we prioritize clean code, balanced workloads, and a polished final pitch. summary:
VitalDrift is an offline-first health monitoring dashboard that helps astronauts on long-duration missions spot changes in their own bodies. Space radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a closed environment can cause immune changes, bone loss, cardiovascular problems and behavioral health issues, and on deep-space missions astronauts must catch these early without real-time help from Earth.

Instead of fixed "normal" ranges, VitalDrift learns each astronaut's personal baseline during the first 14 days. It then tracks drift in resting heart rate, HRV, body temperature, sleep, exercise, mood, reaction time and radiation dose. Each of five body systems (Radiation, Immune, Bone/Muscle, Cardio, Behavioral) shows a simple green, yellow or red light. A "Why?" button explains every flag in plain English, and action cards tell the astronaut what to do next. Several small drifts together raise the alert level, for example fever plus poor sleep plus high heart rate.

The app includes a 90-day mission simulation with injected health problems, a daily check-in, and a summary that can be sent to ground control when a link is available.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VitalDrift builds a personal health baseline for each astronaut from the first 14 days of data, then watches for drift using a simple rule: drift = (today - baseline average) / baseline spread. Drift above 1 gives a YELLOW flag and above 2 gives a RED flag. If two or more indicators in related systems turn yellow, that system is upgraded to RED.

BODY SYSTEMS TRACKED

- Radiation: cumulative dose

- Immune: body temperature, resting heart rate, symptom self-report

- Bone/Muscle: exercise minutes and resistive load

- Cardio: heart rate, HRV

- Behavioral: sleep, mood, reaction time

KEY FEATURES

- Traffic-light dashboard, readable at a glance

- "Why?" explanations in plain English

- Action cards with next steps

- Trend charts with the personal baseline band

- 90-day mission playback with injected problems (stress, infection, bone-loading decline)

- Daily private check-in

- Offline-first: data stays in local storage and a summary can be sent to ground when a link is available

IMPACT

Astronauts become the first line of detection, which matters when communication with Earth is delayed. The same approach could support remote or isolated environments on Earth.

TOOLS

React, Tailwind CSS, browser localStorage, simulated 90-day astronaut dataset. Built with Google AI Studio (Gemini).
